foundation.definition: The strong lowest part of a building that supports everything above it.

column.definition: A regular newspaper article written by the same writer.

beam.definition: Long thick piece of wood or metal or concrete, etc., used in construction.

wall.definition: Anything that suggests a wall in structure or function or effect.

floor.definition: The inside lower horizontal surface (as of a room, hallway, tent, or other structure).

roof.definition: The inner top surface of a covered area or hollow space.

staircase.definition: A way of access (upward and downward) consisting of a set of steps.

elevator-shaft.definition: A tall, enclosed space in a building allows an elevator to travel between its floors.

load-bearing-wall.definition: A wall designed to support weight from parts of a building above it in addition to its own weight.
load-bearing-wall.exampleUsage: The engineer identified the load-bearing wall before the renovation.

truss.definition: (architecture) a triangular bracket of brick or stone (usually of slight extent).

concrete.definition: A hard building material used for paths and surfaces.

steel.definition: A strong metal used to build and support structures.

brick.definition: A small rectangular block used to build walls.

stone.definition: Building material consisting of a piece of rock hewn in a definite shape for a special purpose.

aluminum.definition: A silvery ductile metallic element found primarily in bauxite.

insulation.definition: The state of being isolated or detached.

drywall.definition: A board material used to make the inside walls of a building.

rebar.definition: Steel bars placed inside concrete to make it stronger.

pouring-foundation.definition: The construction stage in which concrete is placed into prepared forms to create a building foundation.
pouring-foundation.exampleUsage: The crew scheduled the foundation pour after the forms were inspected.

framing.definition: Formulation of the plans and important details.

roofing.definition: Material used to construct a roof.

plumbing.definition: The occupation of a plumber (installing and repairing pipes and fixtures for water or gas or sewage in a building).

electrical.definition: Relating to or concerned with electricity.

drywall-installation.definition: The process of fitting and fastening gypsum wallboard to interior wall or ceiling framing.
drywall-installation.exampleUsage: Drywall installation began after the wiring inspection.

painting.definition: A picture made with paint and shown on a wall.

flooring.definition: The inside lower horizontal surface (as of a room, hallway, tent, or other structure).

general-contractor.definition: The lead contractor manages an entire construction project by arranging materials, hiring and overseeing subcontractors, setting the schedule, and ensuring the work meets the design and building laws.

foreman.definition: A person who supervises a group of workers.

carpenter.definition: A skilled worker who builds and repairs things made of wood.

electrician.definition: A skilled worker who installs and repairs electrical systems.

plumber.definition: A skilled worker who installs and repairs water pipes.

mason.definition: A craftsman who works with stone or brick.

ironworker.definition: A person who makes articles of iron.

crane-operator.definition: A person who operates a crane.

surveyor.definition: An engineer who determines the boundaries and elevations of land or structures.

safety-inspector.definition: A professional who checks a workplace or construction site for compliance with safety requirements.
safety-inspector.exampleUsage: The safety inspector reviewed the site barriers and protective equipment.
